topics.title: Meaning, Characteristics, Importance and Principles of Directing
topics.ncert_sections: Meaning; Importance of Directing; Principles of Directing

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the meaning of directing and its characteristics: it initiates action, is continuous, takes place at every level and flows from top to bottom.
Explain how directing initiates action, integrates efforts, realises potential, eases change and brings stability.
Apply the principles of directing such as unity of command, harmony of objectives and appropriateness of direction technique.

topics.title: Elements of Directing and Supervision
topics.ncert_sections: Elements of Direction; Supervision; Importance of Supervision

concepts.learning_objective: Identify supervision, motivation, leadership and communication as the four elements of directing.
Distinguish supervision as an element of directing from supervision as the function of the supervisor at the operative level.
Explain the roles of a supervisor such as linking workers and management, maintaining group unity and training workers.

topics.title: Motivation: Concepts, Features, Process and Importance
topics.ncert_sections: Motivation; Features of Motivation; Motivation Process; Importance of Motivation

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish between a motive, motivation and a motivator.
Explain the features of motivation and the sequence of the motivation process from unsatisfied need to reduction of tension.
Explain how motivation improves performance, changes attitudes and reduces turnover, absenteeism and resistance to change.

topics.title: Maslow's Need Hierarchy Theory
topics.ncert_sections: Maslow's Need Hierarchy Theory of Motivation

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the five levels of needs in Maslow's hierarchy with their organisational examples.
Apply the assumptions of Maslow's theory to explain why a satisfied need no longer motivates.
Identify financial incentives such as pay, bonus, profit sharing, stock options, retirement benefits and perquisites.
Identify non-financial incentives such as status, job enrichment, recognition, job security and empowerment, and explain their basis.

topics.title: Leadership
topics.ncert_sections: Leadership; Features and Importance of Leadership; Leadership Style

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the meaning, features and importance of leadership in an organisation.
Distinguish autocratic, democratic and laissez-faire leadership styles on the basis of the use of authority.

topics.title: Communication: Process, Formal and Informal Communication
topics.ncert_sections: Communication; Elements of Communication Process; Formal and Informal Communication

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the elements of the communication process such as encoding, media, decoding, feedback and noise.
Classify formal communication as upward, downward or horizontal and identify formal communication networks.
Explain the nature of informal (grapevine) communication and its networks.

topics.title: Barriers to Communication and Improving Communication Effectiveness
topics.ncert_sections: Barriers to Communication; Improving Communication Effectiveness

concepts.learning_objective: Identify semantic barriers such as technical jargon, unclarified assumptions and faulty translations.
Classify psychological, organisational and personal barriers to communication.
Suggest measures such as ensuring feedback to improve communication effectiveness.
